learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods.

Possess experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to design experiments and to describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data by combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to solve problems.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Develop, manage, and lead projects that use techniques, tools, and methodologies typical of data science in different application areas.
Identify opportunities for innovative data-oriented applications in continuously evolving technological environments.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Utilize software engineering techniques for the management, analysis, design, and development of products that require intensive use of data.
Integrate into a software development team to build it according to client needs.
Know the main process models and methodologies for developing software products.
Analyze stakeholder needs and specify requirements, interacting effectively with the client.
Organize and distribute work within a team and monitor its progress.
Understand basic concepts of software quality and testing.
Perform effective tests on software components during their development.
Understand basic concepts of software configuration management.
Use version control tools during software development.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Software Development Processes. Frameworks and Software Development Methodologies: Structured and Agile. Scrum and Kanban.
Requirements Elicitation and Analysis. Representation and models. Functionality and data.
Introduction to Software Testing. Basic testing techniques.
Team development, for a given client, of a software product related to the storage, processing, and presentation of data to the user.

assessment_methods.method: Software product development (continuous evaluation of team project work)
Software product development (evaluation of student's contribution in reports, products, deliverables, and final presentation)
Attendance to in-person laboratory practical classes (at least 80% attendance)
Completion of tasks and activities on the virtual campus

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum of 4 points out of 10 is required on both the theory exam and the software product development. If this requirement is met, the final grade is a weighted average: theory exam (40%), software product development (40%), and attendance/participation (20%); otherwise, the maximum grade is 4 points. For the extraordinary call, theory exam and software product development grades from the ordinary call are used if they are at least 5 out of 10; otherwise, new evaluations are conducted. Attendance and participation grades carry over. A minimum of 5 points out of 10 is required for both the theory exam and software product development in the extraordinary call; if met, the final grade is a weighted average as above; otherwise, the maximum grade is 4 points.
